'''Nai Phuan Ong''' (born 10 September 1948 in [[Penang]], [[Malaysia]]) is an American experimental physicist, specializing in "condensed matter physics focusing on [[topological insulator]]s, Dirac/Weyl [[semimetals]], [[superconductor]]s and [[quantum spin liquid]]s."<ref name=NAS>{{cite web|title=Nai Phuan Ong|website=National Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/nai-phuan-ong-czxcdm/}}</ref>

==Biography==
Nai Phuan Ong was born in Penang, Malaysia to parents of Chinese origin on 10 September 1948.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Physics |first=American Institute of |date=2022-04-14 |title=Nai Phuan Ong |url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/47203 |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=www.aip.org |language=en}}</ref> He grew up speaking a Chinese dialect with his parents and English with his seven siblings.<ref name=":0" /> As a youth, he attended [[St. Xavier's Institution|Saint Xaviers Institution]], run by the Christian Brothers, where classes were taught in English.<ref name=":0" /> His interest in science was spurred by his sister's library books; he started going to the library himself at the age of ten and read books about science and airplanes, fascinated to learn how they fly. He started building toy airplanes and copying drawings of turbine blades and pistons in jet engines.<ref name=":0" /> 

Ong immigrated to the United States with his family in 1967. He won a scholarship to [[Columbia College (New York)|Columbia College]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Comment Wall |url=https://scholar.princeton.edu/phuanfest70/comment-wall |access-date=2022-10-08 |website=scholar.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref> the oldest undergraduate college of Columbia University, and graduated from there in 1971 with a B.A. in physics. He went on to complete a Ph.D., in 1976,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bio|url=https://scholar.princeton.edu/phuanfest70/bio|access-date=2021-05-22|website=scholar.princeton.edu|language=en}}</ref> under the direction of [[Alan M. Portis|Alan Portis]], from the [[University of California, Berkeley]]. At the [[University of Southern California]], Ong was an assistant professor from 1976 to 1982, an associate professor 1982 to 1984, and a full professor in 1985. He joined the faculty at [[Princeton University]] as the first Asian professor in 1985.<ref name=":0" /> In 2003, he was appointed to the [[Eugene Higgins]] Professorship of Physics,<ref>{{cite web|title=Happer and Ong named to endowed professorships|website=Princeton University|url=https://pr.princeton.edu/pwb/03/0224/2b.shtml}}</ref> which he continues to hold. Ong was a member of the editorial board of the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' from January 2012 to February 2014.

He has been the advisor for many doctoral students, including [[Harold Y. Hwang]], and many post-docs, including [[Kathryn Moler]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nai Phuan Ong, Professor|website=Physics Tree (academictree.org)|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=80824}}</ref>

In 1982 Ong married Delicia Lai (born 1960).

==Research==
In the 1970s and 1980s Ong did important research on charge-density waves.<ref name="Monçeau Ong Portis Meerschaut pp. 602–606">{{cite journal | last1=Monçeau | first1=P. | last2=Ong | first2=N. P. | last3=Portis | first3=A. M. | last4=Meerschaut | first4=A. | last5=Rouxel | first5=J. | title=Electric Field Breakdown of Charge-Density-Wave—Induced Anomalies in NbSe3 | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=37 | issue=10 | date=6 September 1976 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.37.602 | pages=602–606| bibcode=1976PhRvL..37..602M }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=N. P. |last1=Ong |first2=G. |last2=Verma |first3=K. |last3=Maki |title=Vortex-Array Model for Charge-Density-Wave Conduction Noise |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=52 |issue=8 |date=1984-02-20 |pages=663–666 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.663|bibcode=1984PhRvL..52..663O }}</ref> After the discovery of high temperature superconductivity, Ong worked on transport phenomena in cuprate semiconductors.<ref name="Ong Wang Clayhold Tarascon pp. 8807–8810">{{cite journal | last1=Ong | first1=N. P. | last2=Wang | first2=Z. Z. | last3=Clayhold | first3=J. | last4=Tarascon | first4=J. M. | last5=Greene | first5=L. H. | last6=McKinnon | first6=W. R. | title=Hall effect ofLa2−xSrxCuO4: Implications for the electronic structure in the normal state | journal=Physical Review B | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=35 | issue=16 | date=1 June 1987 | issn=0163-1829 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.35.8807 | pages=8807–8810| pmid=9941259 | bibcode=1987PhRvB..35.8807O }}</ref><ref name="Chien Wang Ong 1991 pp. 2088–2091">{{cite journal | last1=Chien | first1=T. | last2=Wang | first2=Z. | last3=Ong | first3=N. | title=Effect of Zn impurities on the normal-state Hall angle in single-crystal YBa_{2}Cu_{3-x}Zn_{x}O_{7-δ} | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=67 | issue=15 | year=1991 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.67.2088 | pages=2088–2091| pmid=10044332 }}</ref> In recent years, Ong has done research on Dirac and Weyl semimetals, the thermal [[Hall effect]], and [[Majorana fermion|topological superconductors]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://phy.princeton.edu/people/nai-phuan-ong | title = Nai Phuan Ong {{!}} Department of Physics |website=Princeton University}}</ref>

{{blockquote|In 2000, Ong’s group found that the cuprate pair condensate survives to temperatures high above [[Curie temperature|''T''<sub>C</sub>]]. The loss of superconductivity at ''T''<sub>C</sub> arises from the collapse of phase rigidity rather than the closing of a gap. However, its existence is betrayed by a large [[Nernst effect]] and a large orbital [[diamagnetism]]. In topological matter, Ong with [[Robert Cava|Bob Cava]] detected (2010) surface Dirac states in the topological insulator Bi<sub>2</sub>Te<sub>3</sub> by measuring quantum oscillations in a tilted magnetic field. In 2014, Ong and Cava obtained evidence for the predicted "chiral anomaly" in the Dirac semimetals Na<sub>3</sub>Bi and GdPtBi. In several frustrated quantum magnets, Ong’s group has found that spin excitations produce a large thermal Hall current despite being strictly charge-neutral.<ref name=NAS/>}}

==Awards and honors==
* 1982–1984  — Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship
* 1989 — elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], "For research on transport properties of low-dimensional systems, especially the phenomena of sliding charge-density waves"<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1989&unit_id=&institution=Princeton+University}}</ref>
* 2006 — [[H. Kamerlingh Onnes Prize]] (shared with Hidenori Takagi and Shin-ichi Uchida) "for pioneering and seminal transport experiments which illuminated the unconventional nature of the metallic state of high temperature superconducting cuprates"<ref>{{cite web |url=http://kamerlingh-onnes-prize.ch/ |title=Kamerlingh Onnes Prize }}</ref>
* 2006 — elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Book of Members 1780 – Present, Chapter O|website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences (amacad.org)|url=https://www.amacad.org/sites/default/files/academy/multimedia/pdfs/publications/bookofmembers/ChapterO.pdf}}</ref>
* 2010 — Lecturer in Distinguished Lecture Series, Lewiner Institute for Theoretical Physics, [[Technion]], Haifa (3 lectures on cuprates and topological insulators), April 28-May 4, 2010<ref>{{cite web|title=All Distinguished Lecture Series|website=Lewiner Institute for Theoretical Physics|url=https://litp.technion.ac.il/index.php/distinguished-lectures}}</ref>
* 2010 — elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]
*2012 — elected a Member of the U.S. National Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite web | title = FACULTY AWARD: Four Princeton faculty elected to National Academy of Sciences | website = Princeton University | date = | url = https://www.princeton.edu/news/2012/05/07/faculty-award-four-princeton-faculty-elected-national-academy-sciences}}</ref>
*2014 — Experimental Investigators in Quantum Materials Award from [[Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation]]
*2014–2018  — listed among Thomas Reuters Highly Cited Researchers
